<a id="tool-query_planning"></a>
## `query_planning` — Query Planning

**Custom Resource trigger** → if user prompt names a production support role NOT in the standard productionTeam (Photographer/Stylist/Model/Art Director/Hair&Makeup/Assistant/Videographer/DigitalProcessing) → call this tool with `includeCustomResources=true`. Common triggers: 'cater', 'lunch', 'runner', 'driver', 'PA', 'DIT', 'dog handler', 'medic' (and any similar free-form role). Custom Resource labels are FREE-FORM text studios type themselves → semantic-match them yourself from `customResourceLabelsAvailable[]` + `customResources[]` in the response. **Tool-first, ask-later**: call the tool, then if `customResourceLabelsAvailable=[]` ask user; otherwise semantic-match from availableLabels. **Trailing-junk / cut-off tolerance**: if user prompt has trailing backslash (`\`), ellipsis (`...`), question marks (`??`), or appears truncated mid-word, IGNORE the noise and treat the readable trigger word as the query. Do NOT respond with 'your message looks cut off' — call the tool with the cleaned query. Examples: 'Who is today's Cater' → query for cater. 'Lunch...' → query for lunch. 'DIT??' → query for DIT. **Likely-misread tolerance**: if a trigger word could be misread as a proper noun (e.g. 'Cater' → 'Carter', 'DIT' → a person's initials), DEFAULT to the production-role interpretation (this tool is in a production planning context, not a general-knowledge chat). Don't suggest sports/celebrity readings of trigger words. **Default 'today' to ISO date**: when user says 'today', 'hôm nay', 'this morning', etc., automatically set `dateFrom`=`dateTo`=current date in `YYYY-MM-DD`, computed in the USER's timezone (see `_userSettings` in prior tool results) — NOT UTC. Same for 'tomorrow' (+1 day), 'yesterday' (-1 day), 'this week' (Mon-Sun current week). Pass date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` values: the server interprets each date's day boundaries in the user's timezone, so no manual UTC offset is needed. Don't ask the user to specify the date when they used a relative phrase. Search planning sessions — scheduled production shoots with team, time slots, and progress. Use this to answer: what's planned, when (ISO 8601 UTC), where, who's on set, sample check-in status, photography progress, alerts. **Who-is-working queries**: when user asks 'who is working this week', 'which talent has sessions today', 'list photographers on sessions next month' → set `groupByTeamMember=true` with `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Response flips to person-centric: each entry shows the team member with their sessions. This is the primary way to answer talent-on-session questions when the studio does not use the Resource Booking add-on. Filter by team member (any role) or specific role (photographer, stylist, model, art director, assistant, videographer, hair & makeup). Also filter by sessionCode (e.g. 'SES137123CF'), sessionName (partial), sessionDescription (exact), location, production type, check-in/alert/photography status, date range. Supports custom property filters via customPropertyFilters (JSON array of {name, value} for exact match or {name, from, to} for a Date range. Number-type properties also support a comparison operator (eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte/between/notBetween) mirroring the UI — see the customPropertyFilters param for the exact shape). CUSTOM PROPERTIES: each session's `customProperties` lists only properties that have a value SET. A property name being absent from a session does NOT mean it is undefined — it may be defined-but-unset. Before telling the user a custom property does not exist (or is missing) for sessions, call query_property(entityType='session') to get the full list of properties defined for this studio; never conclude a property is undefined from a query_planning result alone. Filter by associated job (jobCode/jobName, or `job` ambiguous = code OR name) and product attributes (productCode/productName, or `product` ambiguous = code OR name, plus brand, category, color, styleCode) — exact match, case-insensitive, matches if ANY of the session's jobs/products satisfies the filter. Editorial workflow: filter by associated project (projectCode/projectName, or `project` ambiguous = code OR name, plus campaign) and deliverable (deliverableCode/deliverableName, or `deliverable` ambiguous = code OR name, plus deliverableOutputName) — exact match, case-insensitive, matches if ANY of the session's projects/deliverables satisfies the filter. Use `user` to find a session where a given user is on the production team regardless of skill/role (V2 ProductionTeams). Returns: session `id` (UUID), sessionName, sessionCode, time slots (ISO 8601 UTC), full production team (resolved names), check-in status, photography progress, job codes, product codes. When groupBy params set, returns counts/aggregations instead of list. **Session lookup param choice — strict per user phrasing:**   • User says 'session code SES137123CF' / 'code SES…' → `sessionCode` only.   • User says 'session named Nike Spring' / 'the Spring shoot' → `sessionName` only.   • User says 'session SES137123CF' / 'session Nike Spring' WITHOUT specifying code-vs-name → `session` (ambiguous param, matches code OR name OR UUID). Don't pass multiple session params at once — pick the one that matches user intent. **Chain with query_talent_crew_schedule**: when the user asks about bookings/holds for a specific session, FIRST call this tool → take response's `id` and `timeSlots` → pass to `query_talent_crew_schedule(sessionId=&lt;id&gt;, dateFrom=&lt;min start&gt;, dateTo=&lt;max end&gt;, ...)`. **Custom Resource queries** (cater / catering / lunch / food / runner / driver / transport / PA / production assistant / makeup artist (one-off) / any role NOT in standard productionTeam): set `includeCustomResources=true`. Custom resources are free-form (label, name) pairs attached inline to a session via the FE 'CUSTOM RESOURCE' panel → free-form means studios type whatever they want ('cater', 'Cater', 'catering', 'lunch', 'food service'). The tool returns ALL custom resources on the page and Claude does the semantic match (no server-side filter — too many false-negatives on free-form text like 'Caster' vs 'cater'). **Semantic match rule** (CRITICAL for custom resources): the response includes `customResourceLabelsAvailable: string[]` → distinct labels seen on the page, plus `customResources[{label,name}]` per session. Scan `customResourceLabelsAvailable` for labels **semantically similar** to the user's word, then read the matching `customResources` entries. DO NOT reply 'not found' until you've checked every label. Examples: 'cater' → look for 'catering', 'lunch', 'meal', 'food service', 'snack runner'; 'driver' → 'transport', 'shuttle', 'logistics'; 'PA' → 'production assistant', 'runner', 'gopher'. Tell the user which labels you considered (e.g. 'No exact 'cater' label, but 'catering' is set to John Smith → likely the same role.'). **Custom resource has NO booking status** (no Confirmed/Hold) → it's session-inline data, not a resource booking. Don't mention status pills for these rows. TEXT FILTERS — these params accept inline operators (sessionDescription): Plain text = exact match (case-insensitive). Supports inline operators (case-insensitive): 'isNotEmpty' (has any value), 'isEmpty' (no value), 'contains:foo', 'notContains:foo', 'ne:foo' (not equal), 'eq:foo' (exact). E.g. to find records where this field has a value, pass 'isNotEmpty'.

- **CF module:** Planning
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no

**Parameters**

<details>
<summary>Show all 50 parameters</summary>

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|:--------:|-------------|
| `sessionName` | string | no | Session name — wildcard contains, case-insensitive (e.g. 'Nike Spring' matches 'Nike Spring Shoot 2026'). Use when the user explicitly says the session NAME. |
| `sessionCode` | string | no | Session code — exact match (e.g. 'SES137123CF', case-insensitive). Use when the user explicitly says the session CODE. Response's `id` is the session UUID needed by query_talent_crew_schedule. |
| `session` | string | no | Session identifier when the user said something like 'session X' WITHOUT specifying it's a name or code. Server matches X against EITHER sessionCode OR sessionName (wildcard). Don't use this if the user explicitly called it a code or a name — pass `sessionCode` or `sessionName` instead. |
| `sessionDescription` | string | no | Session description filter (text — supports inline operators, see TEXT FILTERS in the tool description). |
| `dateFrom` | string | no | Time slot start date from (ISO or epoch ms) |
| `dateTo` | string | no | Time slot start date to (ISO or epoch ms) |
| `location` | string | no | Location/set name or ID |
| `productionType` | string | no | Production type name or ID |
| `teamMember` | string | no | Team member name or user ID (any role — finds person in any team position) |
| `user` | string | no | User name or user ID — finds person on the session's V2 ProductionTeams regardless of skill/role. Use this when the caller says 'user X' without specifying a role. |
| `photographer` | string | no | Photographer name or user ID |
| `stylist` | string | no | Stylist name or user ID |
| `model` | string | no | Model name or user ID |
| `artDirector` | string | no | Art director name or user ID |
| `assistant` | string | no | Assistant name or user ID |
| `videographer` | string | no | Videographer name or user ID |
| `hairAndMakeup` | string | no | Hair & makeup artist name or user ID |
| `jobCode` | string | no | Job code on the session — exact match, case-insensitive (matches if any of the session's jobs has this code) |
| `jobName` | string | no | Job name on the session — exact match, case-insensitive |
| `job` | string | no | Job identifier when the caller said 'job X' WITHOUT specifying code-vs-name — matches against jobCode OR jobName. |
| `productCode` | string | no | Product code on the session — exact match, case-insensitive (matches if any of the session's products has this code) |
| `productName` | string | no | Product name on the session — exact match, case-insensitive |
| `product` | string | no | Product identifier when the caller said 'product X' WITHOUT specifying code-vs-name — matches against productCode OR productName. |
| `brand` | string | no | Product brand on the session — exact match, case-insensitive |
| `category` | string | no | Product category on the session — exact match, case-insensitive |
| `color` | string | no | Product color on the session — exact match, case-insensitive |
| `styleCode` | string | no | Product style code on the session — exact match, case-insensitive |
| `projectCode` | string | no | Editorial project code on the session — exact match, case-insensitive (matches if any of the session's projects has this code) |
| `projectName` | string | no | Editorial project name on the session — exact match, case-insensitive |
| `project` | string | no | Editorial project identifier when the caller said 'project X' WITHOUT specifying code-vs-name — matches against projectCode OR projectName. |
| `campaign` | string | no | Editorial project campaign on the session — exact match, case-insensitive |
| `deliverableCode` | string | no | Editorial deliverable code on the session — exact match, case-insensitive (matches if any of the session's deliverables has this code) |
| `deliverableName` | string | no | Editorial deliverable name on the session — exact match, case-insensitive |
| `deliverable` | string | no | Editorial deliverable identifier when the caller said 'deliverable X' WITHOUT specifying code-vs-name — matches against deliverableCode OR deliverableName. |
| `deliverableOutputName` | string | no | Editorial deliverable output name on the session — exact match, case-insensitive |
| `allCheckedIn` | bool? | no | Only sessions with all items checked in |
| `hasAlerts` | bool? | no | Only sessions with alerts |
| `photographyDone` | bool? | no | Only sessions where photography is done |
| `workspace` | string | no | Workspace/client ID |
| `groupByLocation` | bool | no | Group by location — aggregation mode |
| `groupByProductionType` | bool | no | Group by production type — aggregation mode |
| `groupByPeriod` | string | no | Group by period: day, week, month — aggregation mode |
| `groupByWorkspace` | bool | no | Group by workspace/client — aggregation mode. Use for any 'per workspace', 'per client', 'by workspace' question. |
| `groupByTeamMember` | bool | no | Group results by team member instead of by session. Returns `teamMembers[]` — each entry has `userId`, `userName`, `skillName`, `sessionCount`, and `sessions[]` (code, name, timeSlots). Use when the user asks WHO is working in a date range (e.g. 'who is working this week', 'which photographers have sessions next month', 'list all talent on sessions today'). This is the primary tool for talent-on-session queries when the studio does not use the Resource Booking add-on. All other filters (dateFrom, dateTo, photographer, skill roles, location, etc.) still apply — this only changes the response shape from session-centric to person-centric. |
| `pageSize` | int | no | Max results (ignored in aggregation) |
| `page` | int | no | Page (0-based, ignored in aggregation) |
| `customPropertyFilters` | string | no | JSON array of custom property filters. Each item: {"name":"PropertyName","value":"exact value"} for exact match, or {"name":"PropertyName","from":"2025-12-01","to":"2025-12-31"} for a date range. The sub-field (.number / .keylower / epoch-ms date) is chosen automatically from the property value type. An optional `operator` (case-insensitive — notContains, NOTCONTAINS, notcontains all work; mirrors the UI) refines the match. The valid operators depend on the property's value type: NUMBER: eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, notBetween, isEmpty, isNotEmpty — single-bound (eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte) read `value` (e.g. {"name":"Qty","operator":"gt","value":"1"}); between/notBetween read `from`+`to`; when omitted: value⇒eq, from+to⇒between, from⇒gte, to⇒lte. Always pass plain numeric strings, never dates. TEXT and LIST-of-options: eq, ne, contains, notContains, isEmpty, isNotEmpty — eq/ne/contains/notContains read `value` (e.g. {"name":"Notes","operator":"contains","value":"urgent"}); when omitted, value⇒eq. For LIST-of-options, `value` must match a defined option label. DATE: use `from`/`to` for the range (convert relative ranges like 'last 30 days' to absolute dates yourself); operators are not applied to dates. isEmpty/isNotEmpty need no value (filter on whether the property is set). Pick the form that matches the property's value type — a Number filter with date values, or an operator that doesn't fit the type, is silently dropped and returns wrong results. Example: [{"name":"Season","value":"SS26"},{"name":"item_count","operator":"between","from":"1","to":"10"},{"name":"notes","operator":"contains","value":"rush"}] |
| `customPropertyName` | string | no | Custom property name (resolved to GUID) or GUID directly. Used with groupByCustomProperty for aggregation. |
| `groupByCustomProperty` | bool | no | Group by the value of customPropertyName — aggregation mode. Requires customPropertyName to be set. |
| `includeCustomResources` | bool | no | Include `customResources: [{label, name}]` per session AND `customResourceLabelsAvailable: string[]` (distinct labels seen on this page) in the response. Default false (saves 1 batch round-trip to /sessions/enrich). Pass true when the user prompt mentions a role NOT in the standard productionTeam list (Photographer/Stylist/Model/Art Director/Hair&Makeup/Assistant/Videographer/DigitalProcessing) — e.g. cater, catering, lunch, food, runner, driver, transport, PA, production assistant. Custom resources have NO booking status — they're inline session data, not bookings. |

</details>

**Example input**

```json
{ "dateFrom": "2026-06-01", "dateTo": "2026-06-30", "location": "Studio A", "pageSize": 10 }
```

**Example output**

```json
{ "total": 7, "hits": [ { "sessionId": "p1...", "sessionName": "SS26 Day 1", "date": "2026-06-12", "location": "Studio A" } ] }
```

**Known limitations**

Time slots are stored as epoch ms and returned as ISO 8601. Non-standard production-support roles are only included when includeCustomResources is set.

<a id="tool-query_post_production_vendors"></a>
## `query_post_production_vendors` — Query Post-Production Vendors

List external post-production vendor connections configured in the studio. External post-production vendors are third-party services integrated into the workflow to handle image/video retouching and editing after the shoot. Connector types: FTP/SFTP, Pixelz, Box.com, Bright River, Gateway API. Each vendor shows its connection type and last connection check status. Supports pagination, keyword search, and vendor type filter.

- **CF module:** Studio Settings
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|:--------:|-------------|
| `keyword` | string | no | Text search by vendor name. |
| `pageSize` | int | no | Items per page (default 50). |
| `page` | int | no | Page number, 1-based (default 1). |
| `vendorType` | string | no | Filter by vendor type name or ID. Values: FTP, PIXELZ Integration, Box.com, Bright River Integration, Gateway API. |

**Example input**

```json
{ "vendorType": "Pixelz", "pageSize": 10 }
```

**Example output**

```json
{ "total": 2, "items": [ { "name": "Pixelz Retouch", "id": "pv1...", "type": "PIXELZ Integration", "lastCheckSuccess": true, "lastCheckDate": "2026-07-05T12:00:00Z", "lastCheckError": null } ] }
```

**Known limitations**

External post-production vendors are third-party retouching/editing services wired into the workflow. Lists the vendor connections + last connection-check status only — not the images they process (use query_asset / query_ecomm_production). Connector types: FTP/SFTP, Pixelz, Box.com, Bright River, Gateway API. Distinct from query_product_vendors (image capture, not post-production).

<a id="tool-query_presets"></a>
## `query_presets` — Query Presets

List presets configured in the studio. Presets define output specifications for images and videos — file format, DPI, dimensions, color profile, cropping, etc. Each preset has variants (up to 50) that deliver multiple image outputs with different specs from a single position. Media types: Photo, Video. Configured per workspace and assigned to Style Guide positions. Use 'type' param: ecomm (default) or editorial (add-on, not all studios have it). Supports pagination, keyword search, and workspace filter.

- **CF module:** Studio Settings
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|:--------:|-------------|
| `type` | string | no | Preset type to query. Values: ecomm, editorial. Default: ecomm. |
| `keyword` | string | no | Text search by preset name. |
| `pageSize` | int | no | Items per page (default 50). |
| `page` | int | no | Page number, 1-based (default 1). |
| `workspace` | string | no | Filter by workspace/client name or ID. |

**Example input**

```json
{ "type": "ecomm", "workspace": "Acme Studio", "pageSize": 10 }
```

**Example output**

```json
{ "total": 12, "items": [ { "name": "Web JPG 2000px", "id": "pr1...", "presetType": "ecomm", "mediaType": "Photo", "workspace": "Acme Studio", "numberOfVariants": 3 } ] }
```

**Known limitations**

Presets define output specs (format, DPI, dimensions, color profile, cropping) and are assigned to Style Guide positions. Set `type`: ecomm (default) or editorial. Editorial is an add-on — if the studio lacks the Editorial Projects feature it silently returns nothing for editorial. Media types: Photo, Video. `numberOfVariants` = configured output variants (ecomm) / deliverables (editorial).

<a id="tool-query_product_vendors"></a>

List product vendors configured in the studio. Product vendors are external teams that capture/provide product imagery via the Vendor Portal — they receive product requests, upload images, and submit them back into the workflow. Each vendor has a request level controlling what they deliver: Final Selection (delivers final chosen images including main/cover picks), Pre-selection (submits candidate images for selection later), Pre-selection By Position (candidate images mapped to specific shot positions e.g. front, back, detail). userCount is the number of vendor user accounts who can log into the Vendor Portal. Supports pagination, keyword search, and filters by enabled status or request level.

- **CF module:** Studio Settings
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no

|------|------|:--------:|-------------|
| `keyword` | string | no | Text search by vendor name. |
| `pageSize` | int | no | Items per page (default 50). |
| `page` | int | no | Page number, 1-based (default 1). |
| `isEnabled` | bool? | no | Filter by enabled/disabled status. |
| `requestLevel` | string | no | Filter by request level name or ID. Values: Final Selection (1), Pre-selection (2), Pre-selection By Position (3). |

```json
{ "requestLevel": "Final Selection", "isEnabled": true, "pageSize": 10 }
```

**Known limitations**

Product vendors are external teams that capture product imagery via the Vendor Portal. Lists the vendor teams + config only — not the images/products they deliver. `requestLevel` accepts a name or id: Final Selection (1), Pre-selection (2), Pre-selection By Position (3). `userCount` = vendor-portal user accounts. Distinct from query_post_production_vendors (retouching, not capture).

<a id="tool-query_property"></a>
## `query_property` — Query Property

List property definitions for a given entity type in this studio. Returns all properties (both custom and reserved system properties). Each property includes name, internalName, isEditable (true = custom property defined by the studio and can be modified; false = reserved system property that cannot be changed), valueType (Free text, List of options, Date, Date time, Number), and syncMode. COUNTING: when the user asks how many properties match any criteria (a given valueType, syncMode, isEditable flag, or any combination), do NOT count the list by hand — write and run code that filters the returned `properties` array and reports its length. Manual tallying is unreliable.

- **CF module:** Properties

<a id="tool-query_sample"></a>
## `query_sample` — Query Sample

Search samples (physical product items) — track location, check-in/out status, and containers. The only tool that returns actual sample records. Sample records carry editorial PROJECT links only (editorialProjectIds) — NOT deliverable links. For sample↔deliverable questions ('which deliverables use this sample', 'which samples are shared across deliverables', 'list samples assigned to a deliverable'), use query_editorial_production instead: filter by sampleCode/sampleName or deliverableCode/deliverableIds — each work-unit hit returns both its deliverable info and its samples snapshot. Use this to answer: where is a sample, is it checked in, which samples are at a location, which samples are overdue for return, which samples belong to a project, counts by location/status. Samples are linked to editorial projects — use editorialProjectIds to filter samples by project. Check-in status: WaitingForCheckingIn, CheckedIn, CheckedOut. Filter by sample code, barcode, product code, size, job, location, check-in status, workspace, container, container type, product type, label recognition, check-in/out dates, editorialProjectIds. Use human-readable names for location (resolved to IDs automatically). Supports custom property filters via customPropertyFilters (JSON array of {name, value} for exact match or {name, from, to} for a Date range. Number-type properties also support a comparison operator (eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte/between/notBetween) mirroring the UI — see the customPropertyFilters param for the exact shape). CUSTOM PROPERTIES: each sample's `customProperties` lists only properties that have a value SET. A property name being absent from a sample does NOT mean it is undefined — it may be defined-but-unset. Before telling the user a custom property does not exist (or is missing) for samples, call query_property(entityType='sample') to get the full list of properties defined for this studio; never conclude a property is undefined from a query_sample result alone. When any groupBy* param is set, returns aggregation buckets instead of a list. For any 'per workspace' or 'per client' breakdown, use groupByWorkspace=true. TEXT FILTERS — these params accept inline operators (sampleCode, sampleName): Plain text = exact match (case-insensitive). Supports inline operators (case-insensitive): 'isNotEmpty' (has any value), 'isEmpty' (no value), 'contains:foo', 'notContains:foo', 'ne:foo' (not equal), 'eq:foo' (exact). E.g. to find records where this field has a value, pass 'isNotEmpty'.

- **CF module:** Samples
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|:--------:|-------------|

| `location` | string | no | Location/sub-location name or ID. |

| `checkedInDateFrom` | string | no | Earliest sample check-in date. ISO date or epoch ms. |
| `checkedInDateTo` | string | no | Latest sample check-in date. |
| `checkedOutDateFrom` | string | no | Earliest sample check-out date. ISO date or epoch ms. |

Each item: {"name":"PropertyName","value":"exact value"} for exact match, or {"name":"PropertyName","from":"2025-12-01","to":"2025-12-31"} for a date range. The sub-field (.number / .keylower / epoch-ms date) is chosen automatically from the property value type. An optional `operator` (case-insensitive — notContains, NOTCONTAINS, notcontains all work; mirrors the UI) refines the match. The valid operators depend on the property's value type: NUMBER: eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, notBetween, isEmpty, isNotEmpty — single-bound (eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte) read `value` (e.g. {"name":"Qty","operator":"gt","value":"1"}); between/notBetween read `from`+`to`; when omitted: value⇒eq, from+to⇒between, from⇒gte, to⇒lte. Always pass plain numeric strings, never dates. TEXT and LIST-of-options: eq, ne, contains, notContains, isEmpty, isNotEmpty — eq/ne/contains/notContains read `value` (e.g. {"name":"Notes","operator":"contains","value":"urgent"}); when omitted, value⇒eq. For LIST-of-options, `value` must match a defined option label. DATE: use `from`/`to` for the range (convert relative ranges like 'last 30 days' to absolute dates yourself); operators are not applied to dates. isEmpty/isNotEmpty need no value (filter on whether the property is set). Pick the form that matches the property's value type — a Number filter with date values, or an operator that doesn't fit the type, is silently dropped and returns wrong results. Example: [{"name":"Season","value":"SS26"},{"name":"item_count","operator":"between","from":"1","to":"10"},{"name":"notes","operator":"contains","value":"rush"}] |
| `customPropertyName` | string | no | Custom property name (resolved to GUID) or GUID directly. Used with groupByCustomProperty for aggregation. |
| `sampleIds` | JsonElement? | no | Sample GUIDs — drill-down array, e.g. the sampleId values from query_editorial_production sharedSamples buckets. Accepts a JSON array or a JSON-encoded string array. |
| `editorialProjectIds` | JsonElement? | no | Editorial Project IDs — drill-down array from query_editorial_project. |
| `groupByCheckInStatus` | bool | no | Group by check-in status — aggregation mode. |
| `groupByLocation` | bool | no | Group by location — aggregation mode. |
| `groupByWorkspace` | bool | no | Group by workspace/client — aggregation mode. MUST be set for 'per workspace/client' questions. |
| `groupByContainerType` | bool | no | Group by container type — aggregation mode. |
| `groupByCustomProperty` | bool | no | Group by the value of customPropertyName — aggregation mode. Requires customPropertyName to be set. |
| `groupByPeriod` | string | no | Time-bucket aggregation: day, week, or month. Pair with groupByPeriodField. Bucket boundaries follow the user's timezone. Provide the matching date range (checkedInDateFrom/To or checkedOutDateFrom/To) to bound the buckets; unbounded defaults to the last year. |
| `groupByPeriodField` | string | no | Date field driving the time-bucket aggregation: checkedIn (default) or checkedOut. |
| `pageSize` | int | no | Max results (ignored in aggregation). |
| `page` | int | no | Page (0-based, ignored in aggregation). |

</details>

<a id="tool-query_styleguide"></a>
## `query_styleguide` — Query Style Guide

List style guides configured in the studio. A style guide is the set of styling/copywriting rules a client applies to its production work. Returns: id, name, workspace, description, isDefault, isEnabled, isInvalid, isWorkflowEnabled, created, updated, deepLinkUrl (clickable link to the style guide in the web app). **Use cases**: (1) Enumerate which style guides exist for a workspace. (2) Find the default/enabled style guide for a client. (3) Search style guides by name. (4) Surface invalid style guides (isInvalid=true). Pass 'workspace' (name or ID) to scope to one client; omit to list across the studio. Pass 'keyword' for server-side partial name search. Pass 'workflowId' (GUID) OR 'workflowName' to list only style guides bound to a given workflow (workflowName is resolved to a workflow id via search — exact match preferred, ambiguous names return candidates). Pass 'version' (default 2 = current style guides; 1 = legacy). By default the record id is omitted for readability. Pass 'includeIds=true' when the user wants ids — e.g. to then drill into a specific style guide with get_styleguide_detail.

- **CF module:** Style Guides
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no


**Example output**

```json
{ "returned": 2, "hasMore": false, "styleGuides": [ { "id": "2ce383b9-...", "name": "Spring 2026 Apparel", "workspace": "Acme", "isDefault": false, "isEnabled": true, "isInvalid": false, "deepLinkUrl": "https://app.creativeforce-dev.io/settings/styleguides-v2/2ce383b9-..." } ] }
```

List/search style guides only (styling & copywriting rule sets per client) — use get_styleguide_detail to read one guide's full content. The record id is omitted unless includeIds=true (needed to chain into get_styleguide_detail). version defaults to 2 (current); 1 = legacy. Cursor pagination via lastOrderKey = page*pageSize. <a id="tool-query_talent_crew"></a>
## `query_talent_crew` — Query Talent & Crew

Search talent and resource users — both license users (internal team members) and resource users (freelancers, models, agencies). Use this to answer: who is on the team, who has a given skill, what agency a model belongs to, counts of talent by skill / employment type / status. User types: License (internal), Resource (external). Employment types: Permanent, Freelance. States: Enabled, Disabled, NotVerify, Deleted. Common skills: Photographer, Stylist, Model, Art Director, Hair & Makeup, Retoucher, Videographer, Producer, Assistant, Project Manager, Deliverable Owner, Digital Processing. Filter by name, job title, user type, employment type, skill, state, agency, short list, contact info, city, created date range. Supports custom property filters via customPropertyFilters (JSON array of {name, value} for exact match or {name, from, to} for a Date range. Number-type properties also support a comparison operator (eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte/between/notBetween) mirroring the UI — see the customPropertyFilters param for the exact shape). CUSTOM PROPERTIES: each record's `customProperties` lists only properties that have a value SET. A property name being absent from a record does NOT mean it is undefined — it may be defined-but-unset. Before telling the user a custom property does not exist (or is missing) for talent/crew, call query_property(entityType='talent_crew') to get the full list of properties defined for this studio; never conclude a property is undefined from a query_talent_crew result alone. Pass `talentCrewIds` (JSON array of talent crew IDs from query_talent_crew_schedule or other tools) to look up specific records directly instead of re-querying by skill. Use human-readable names for all filters (resolved to IDs automatically). Each record includes a `deepLinkUrl` to the talent detail page in the web app. **CRITICAL — UI rendering ownership**: an inline widget handles record-list and aggregation responses, so your text must NOT duplicate them. Per response shape:   • `hits` with ≥1 talent → widget renders compact-card / table. Text = ONE brief sentence (e.g. 'Found 6 talents in the Christmas 24 short list.').   • Aggregation (`byAgency` / `bySkill` / `byStatus` / `byUserType` / `byEmploymentType`) → widget renders bar-chart sections. Text = ONE brief sentence summarising top buckets (e.g. '15 agencies, top 3: ACME (12), aaa (9), 234234 (8).').   • `hits` empty + `total &gt; 0` (count-only, pageSize=0) → widget HIDES (0 height). Text MUST state the count plainly (e.g. 'Có **123** photographers đang active.').   • `hits` empty + `total = 0` → widget HIDES. Text = brief negative reply (e.g. 'Không có crew member nào match.'). Do NOT write a markdown table, list, gallery, or any field-by-field summary. Do NOT embed `!\[image](avatarUrl)` or `[Show Image](url)`. Do NOT include deep-link URLs in text — the widget already renders the name as a clickable anchor. Avatars are shown by default in compact-card and table views. Pass `includeAvatar=false` only when the caller explicitly wants to skip avatar resolution (e.g. perf-sensitive bulk queries). Still no markdown images in your text — the widget owns the visual. **"Talent" terminology** — `skill="Talent"` is a PSEUDO-SKILL meaning Models + AI Models only (server-side OR-match). ✅ TRIGGER on standalone words: "talent", "talents", "a talent", "the talents", "find a talent", "show me talents", "model agency", or context implying Models specifically. Examples: 'Find a talent named Jane' → { name: 'Jane', skill: 'Talent' }; 'How many talents do we have?' → { skill: 'Talent', pageSize: 0 }. ❌ DO NOT TRIGGER on: 'Talent & Crew' / 'Talent and Crew' / 'talents and crew' — these are the FULL ENTITY NAME (License + Resource = whole pool). They contain the word "Talent" but mean the OPPOSITE — search broad pool, omit `skill`. Examples: 'Find Talent & Crew named Han' → { name: 'Han' } NO skill; 'How many Talent & Crew based in London' → { city: 'London' } NO skill. ❌ DO NOT TRIGGER for explicit roles (Photographers, Stylists, Producers, Hair & Makeup, Videographers, internal team) — pass the explicit skill name or omit the filter. When groupBy params are set, returns counts / aggregations instead of a list. Each hit includes a `rates` array (rateId, name, amount, currency, duration, rateType, agencyFee, payrollFee, isDefault, description) **only if the caller has the `Rates` screen permission**. Top-level `ratesAccess` is `granted` when rates are emitted and `denied` when they are gated out — when `denied`, do not assume the talent has no rates configured, the field is simply hidden by permission. **Rates are sensitive financial data — the widget HIDES them by default.** Even when `ratesAccess=granted` and the `rates` array is populated, the widget does NOT render the rates block in any view (compact card, table drill-down) unless `columns` explicitly includes 'rates'. The schedule tool widget never renders rates. This is a data-minimization safeguard against accidental leaks during screen-shares and casual lookups. To surface rates in the widget, set `columns: ['rates']` (or include 'rates' alongside other columns). You can still reason about rates in your text reply — but only when the user explicitly asked. **STRICT RULE for the `columns` parameter** — you MUST set it whenever the user names specific fields or uses narrowing words ('just', 'only', 'only show', 'just show', 'chỉ', 'chỉ hiển thị', 'khÃ´ng cần'). Do NOT fall back to defaults in those cases. Mapping examples:  • 'List 10 photographers and **just** show their skills' → call with arguments: { skill: 'Photographer', pageSize: 10, columns: ['skills'] }   • '5 models with their **rate info only**' → { skill: 'Model', pageSize: 5, columns: ['rates'] }   • '**Emails and phones** of all stylists' → { skill: 'Stylist', columns: ['email','phone'] }   • 'Which agency does each model belong to' → { skill: 'Model', columns: ['agencies'] }   • 'Talent based in London' → { city: 'London' }   • 'Talent in the Fashion Crew short list' → { shortListName: 'Fashion Crew' }   • 'Talent who are both Photographer AND Videographer' → { skill: 'Photographer|Videographer' }   • 'NotVerify accounts older than 30 days' → { state: 'NotVerify', createdTo: '&lt;today-30d ISO&gt;' }   • 'How many new talents joined in the last 3 months' → { createdFrom: '&lt;today-3m ISO&gt;', pageSize: 0 } (read total)   • 'List talents grouped by skill' (aggregation) → omit columns; the param has no effect on aggregation mode.   • Generic 'list/show me photographers' (no narrowing word) → omit columns; defaults to a broad set. Photo and Name are always rendered as anchors regardless of `columns`. Available column ids: jobTitle, type, employment, status, skills, agencies, email, phone, location, createdAt, pronouns, userCode, rates.

- **CF module:** Talent & Crew
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no

| `groupByStatus` | bool | no | Group by status — aggregation mode |
| `groupByAgency` | bool | no | Group by agency — aggregation mode (nested) |
| `customPropertyFilters` | string | no | JSON array of custom property filters. Each item: {"name":"PropertyName","value":"exact value"} for exact match, or {"name":"PropertyName","from":"2025-12-01","to":"2025-12-31"} for a date range. The sub-field (.number / .keylower / epoch-ms date) is chosen automatically from the property value type. An optional `operator` (case-insensitive — notContains, NOTCONTAINS, notcontains all work; mirrors the UI) refines the match. The valid operators depend on the property's value type: NUMBER: eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, notBetween, isEmpty, isNotEmpty — single-bound (eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte) read `value` (e.g. {"name":"Qty","operator":"gt","value":"1"}); between/notBetween read `from`+`to`; when omitted: value⇒eq, from+to⇒between, from⇒gte, to⇒lte. Always pass plain numeric strings, never dates. TEXT and LIST-of-options: eq, ne, contains, notContains, isEmpty, isNotEmpty — eq/ne/contains/notContains read `value` (e.g. {"name":"Notes","operator":"contains","value":"urgent"}); when omitted, value⇒eq. For LIST-of-options, `value` must match a defined option label. DATE: use `from`/`to` for the range (convert relative ranges like 'last 30 days' to absolute dates yourself); operators are not applied to dates. isEmpty/isNotEmpty need no value (filter on whether the property is set). Pick the form that matches the property's value type — a Number filter with date values, or an operator that doesn't fit the type, is silently dropped and returns wrong results. Example: [{"name":"Season","value":"SS26"},{"name":"item_count","operator":"between","from":"1","to":"10"},{"name":"notes","operator":"contains","value":"rush"}] |
| `customPropertyName` | string | no | Custom property name (resolved to GUID) or GUID directly. Used with groupByCustomProperty for aggregation. |
| `groupByCustomProperty` | bool | no | Group by the value of customPropertyName — aggregation mode. Requires customPropertyName to be set. |
| `pageSize` | int | no | Max results (ignored in aggregation) |
| `page` | int | no | Page (0-based, ignored in aggregation) |
| `includeAvatar` | bool | no | If true (default), eagerly resolve avatarUrl for each hit so the widget renders avatars in compact-card and table views. Pass false only to skip the extra Contact API call. |
| `columns` | JsonElement? | no | Optional. Pick which columns the widget surfaces (applies to BOTH table view and compact card). Choose minimal set based on user intent: ['skills'] for skill questions, ['agencies'] for agency questions, ['email','phone'] for contact questions. **RATES HANDLING — STRICT RULE**: pass `['rates']` ONLY when the user EXPLICITLY mentions rates, cost, pricing, fees, budget, day rate, or asks to compare prices. Do NOT pass `['rates']` for ambiguous prompts like 'show profile', 'who is X', 'tell me about [name]', or for any list/team query that doesn't reference money. Default response (no `columns`) MUST NOT surface rates anywhere — including compact card and detail panel. Available column ids: jobTitle, type, employment, status, skills, agencies, email, phone, location, createdAt, pronouns, userCode, rates. Photo and Name are always shown as anchors. If omitted, defaults to [jobTitle, type, status, skills, agencies] (rates excluded). Aggregation mode ignores `columns`. |
| `view` | string | no | View mode: `widget` (default) renders the avatar table widget; `data` returns the same records under `data[]` with `hits=[]` (widget auto-hides) and SKIPS avatar resolution. **Use `view=data` ONLY when the result is being chained as input to another tool call (intermediate data extraction)**, NOT for user-facing answers. Example chain: extract talent IDs to feed into a follow-up query_talent_crew_schedule(talentCrewIds=[...]) call. Default `widget` is correct for ALL user-facing answers. |

</details>

**Example input**

```json
{ "skill": "Photographer", "city": "London", "pageSize": 10 }
```

**Example output**

```json
{ "total": 8, "hits": [ { "talentCrewId": "t-101", "displayName": "Jane Doe", "jobTitle": "Photographer", "userType": "Resource", "avatarUrl": "https://cdn.../t-101.jpg" } ] }
```

**Known limitations**

Rates are gated by the Rates screen (`ratesAccess: granted|denied`). The pseudo-skill 'Talent' resolves to Model OR AI Model server-side.

<a id="tool-query_talent_crew_schedule"></a>
## `query_talent_crew_schedule` — Query Talent & Crew Schedule

**MANDATORY TRIGGERS** — when user prompt contains ANY of: 'available', 'availability', 'schedule', 'booking', 'confirmed', 'on hold', '1st hold', '2nd hold', 'next week', 'this week', 'on May/June/...', 'free on', 'busy on', 'OOO', 'out of office', 'unavailable on', 'inactive', 'haven't been booked', 'not booked in N days', 'access cleanup', 'dormant', 'idle freelancers' → you MUST call this tool. Do NOT respond with markdown tables, lists, or hallucinate data. The widget will render the answer visually. **Inverse query** (find talents WITHOUT bookings) → use `onlyInactive=true` paired with `dateFrom/dateTo` for the inactivity window. Common phrasings: 'freelancers not booked in 60+ days' → `onlyInactive=true, dateFrom=&lt;60d ago&gt;, dateTo=&lt;today&gt;` (chain with `query_talent_crew(employmentType=Freelancer, view=data)` first to scope pool to freelancers). **NEGATIVE TRIGGER — route to `query_planning` instead** when the prompt names a free-form production SUPPORT role like cater, catering, lunch, food, runner, driver, PA, DIT, dog handler, medic, security, prop master, set decorator, etc. These are NOT skills (skills = Photographer/Stylist/Model/Art Director/Hair&Makeup/Assistant/Videographer/DigitalProcessing). They are Custom Resource labels attached inline to planning sessions. **Do NOT pass them as `skill=...` here → the master skill catalog will not match them and the tool will return 0**. Use `query_planning(includeCustomResources=true)` instead. Query Talent & Crew scheduling data from the Resourcing Calendar — User Availability (Available/OutOfOffice/Unavailable set by the user) and Resource Bookings (1stHold/2ndHold/Confirmed/Unavailable set by manager). Use for: who is available next week, who is confirmed for a shoot date, stale holds, overbooking conflicts, per-record schedule, capacity overview. **This tool ALSO serves as a list view of talents matching the skill filter** — do NOT pre-call query_talent_crew when user prompt combines list+schedule intent (e.g. 'list all Models then their schedule next week'). Pass `skill` directly here for both the list and the schedule in ONE call. **Chain mode**: when the result is being passed as input to another tool (intermediate data extraction, NOT user-facing), set `view=data` to suppress widget render and skip avatar resolution (saves ~150ms). Default `view=widget` is correct for ALL user-facing answers. Requires dateFrom + dateTo. Scope is OPTIONAL. **Do NOT chain via query_talent_crew to pre-resolve IDs by skill.** Pass `skill` directly here — the tool resolves talents internally. When you also pass `availabilityStatus` or `bookingStatus`, the tool runs **status-first**: scans the whole studio crew pool (cap 500), filters by status, then post-filters by skill — this catches talents that a skill-first scope (cap 50) would miss. Use cases for unscoped queries: 'how many crew are unavailable on May 8?' (set pageSize=0 for count-only), 'who is Out of Office next week?'. **Name-scoped queries — mandatory chain.** When the user names a SPECIFIC talent (proper name: 'AloHa NN', 'John Photographer', 'show schedule for Tien'): FIRST call `query_talent_crew(name=..., view=data)` to resolve name → ID(s), then pass those as `talentCrewIds` here. Do NOT call this tool unscoped expecting to find the named talent in the result list — that wastes a round trip and dumps the whole crew on the user. **Session-scoped queries — chain order is mandatory.** When the user mentions a session: FIRST call `query_planning` to resolve the session — pick the right session param: `sessionCode` if user said it's a code, `sessionName` if a name, `session` if ambiguous. Then use the response's `id` (UUID) as `sessionId` here, and `timeSlots` to derive `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Do NOT call this tool first with a raw code/name — it requires a UUID. **Do NOT drop `sessionId` as a fallback** when a session-scoped query returns 0. Zero IS the answer — it means the session has no records matching the filters. Report 0 to the user (e.g. 'no 1st/2nd Hold bookings for that session — the crew are Confirmed instead'). To find out what status the session crew DO have, drop the `bookingStatus` filter while keeping `sessionId` — never the other way around. For session team composition ('who is on session X') use query_planning instead. sessionId here filters bookings linked to a specific session (1st Hold / Confirmed per shoot). Availability statuses (User Availability set by the user): Available, OutOfOffice, Unavailable. Booking statuses (Resource Booking set by manager): typically Option, Contacted, Confirmed, 1st Hold (FirstHold), 2nd Hold (SecondHold), Released, Cancelled, Unavailable — exact list depends on studio config (see _debug.cachedBookingStatusNames). Pass the canonical name (case-insensitive) — server resolves to dynamic statusId. **Multi-status filter — `bookingStatuses` / `availabilityStatuses`**: pass a JSON array of names (e.g. `bookingStatuses=["Confirmed","FirstHold","SecondHold"]`) when the intent covers multiple statuses. Records matching ANY listed status pass. Use the plural form whenever the user phrasing implies a set, not a single canonical status. **Singular vs multi → decide by user word, not by intent**. RULE: if user prompt contains an explicit canonical status word ('confirmed', '1st hold', 'first hold', '2nd hold', 'second hold', 'option', 'contacted', 'released', 'cancelled') → use SINGULAR `bookingStatus=&lt;that word&gt;`. Examples: 'who is **confirmed** today' → `bookingStatus=Confirmed`. 'show me **1st holds** for May 14' → `bookingStatus=FirstHold`. 'anyone **on hold** today' (vague — 1st or 2nd) → `bookingStatuses=["FirstHold","SecondHold"]`. Only use the multi-status form when the user prompt is VAGUE about status: 'who is **working/on-floor/on the books/scheduled/booked** today' → active bookings → `bookingStatuses=["Confirmed","FirstHold","SecondHold"]`. **Heuristic**: if the user typed a status word verbatim, that's the filter → singular. If they typed a generic 'working/scheduled' verb, multi. Don't mix. **Booking-vs-Availability AND-gate (LH-50337 follow-up)**: when ANY booking-status filter is set, the tool now narrows availability records to talents that survived the booking filter (and vice versa). So `bookingStatuses=[...]` will NOT leak availability-only rows for talents without a matching booking. Translation: filtering 'Confirmed today' returns only talents who actually have a Confirmed booking on that day, even though their availability records overlap. When groupBy params set, returns bucket counts instead of list. **Rendering rule**: each record carries a `deepLinkUrl`. When presenting results in text, ALWAYS wrap `displayName` as a clickable markdown link: `[displayName](deepLinkUrl)`. Never print plain names. If `displayName` is empty, fall back to talentCrewId or userCode (still wrapped). **UI rendering**: paired widget renders avatar table with status pills + inline date ranges + clickable names (Availability / Booking / On-set Role columns auto-shown when relevant data present). Per response shape:   • `hits` with ≥1 talent → widget renders compact-card / table. Text = ONE brief sentence summary PLUS optionally ONE useful insight you spot in the data (e.g. 'Found 6 confirmed photographers for May 8 — note: oanh eu has overlapping bookings May 7-15.'). Do not list each row in text — widget shows the data.   • Aggregation (`byAvailabilityStatus` / `byBookingStatus`) → widget renders bar chart. Text = ONE brief sentence summarising buckets.   • `hits` empty + `total &gt; 0` (count-only, pageSize=0) → widget HIDES. Text MUST state the count plainly.   • `hits` empty + `total = 0` → widget HIDES. **IMPORTANT fallback**: before replying 'no one is booked', call `query_planning(dateFrom=&lt;same&gt;, dateTo=&lt;same&gt;, groupByTeamMember=true)` to check if talent are assigned on sessions without bookings. If `query_planning` returns teamMembers, present those results to the user (e.g. 'No bookings found, but these talent are assigned on sessions this week:'). Only reply 'no one is planned' if BOTH tools return empty. **Conflict API unavailability**: if `_debug.conflictApiAvailable === false`, the booking conflict service is down for this query. ALL hits will have `hasConflict=false` regardless of actual state. The widget renders a footer note, but you SHOULD also append a brief warning to your text reply (e.g. 'Note: conflict warnings are temporarily unavailable — verify holds manually'). **INACTIVE BOOKINGS — STRICT RULE**: by default the tool excludes `Cancelled` and `Released` bookings from results (active-schedule hygiene). If `_debug.inactiveCount.total &gt; 0` in the response, the widget rendered fewer rows than exist server-side. Mention this in the text reply (e.g. 'X cancelled / Y released bookings hidden — let me know if you want to see them.'). Pass `includeInactiveBookings=true` ONLY when the user EXPLICITLY mentions cancelled, released, inactive, or 'all bookings' (e.g. 'show all bookings including cancelled', 'were any of Tien's holds released?'). Do NOT pass it for generic 'schedule for X' or 'who's available' queries. **Rates are NEVER shown via this tool.** Schedule queries are about availability and bookings, not pricing. The widget for this tool does not render rates in any view (single, list, or drill-down). If the user asks about rates after a schedule query, chain to `query_talent_crew(talentCrewIds=[&lt;from schedule result&gt;], columns=['rates'])` instead of re-calling the schedule tool. Do NOT write a markdown table, do NOT chain to get_talent_crew_preview, do NOT fabricate avatar URLs in text. Do NOT include deep-link URLs in text — the widget renders the name as a clickable anchor.

- **CF module:** Resourcing Calendar
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no

**Parameters**

<details>
<summary>Show all 18 parameters</summary>

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|:--------:|-------------|
| `talentCrewIds` | JsonElement? | no | Talent crew IDs (JSON array) from query_talent_crew. E.g. ["id1","id2"]. Max 50. |
| `talentCrewId` | string | no | Single talent crew ID — for per-record schedule view. |
| `skill` | string | no | Skill name to scope talent pool e.g. Photographer. Resolved via talentcrew ES. Max 50 results. |
| `dateFrom` | string | no | Start date ISO e.g. 2026-06-01 (required). |
| `dateTo` | string | no | End date ISO e.g. 2026-06-07 (required). |
| `availabilityStatus` | string | no | Filter User Availability status: Available, OutOfOffice, Unavailable. |
| `availabilityStatuses` | JsonElement? | no | Multi-status User Availability filter — JSON array of canonical names, e.g. ["Available","OutOfOffice"]. Records matching ANY listed status pass. Takes precedence over `availabilityStatus` when both supplied. |
| `bookingStatus` | string | no | Filter Resource Booking status — case-insensitive. Common values: Option, Contacted, Confirmed, FirstHold (or '1st Hold'), SecondHold (or '2nd Hold'), Released, Cancelled, Unavailable. Studio-specific list available in _debug.cachedBookingStatusNames. NOTE: by default Cancelled and Released are hidden (data hygiene); pass them explicitly here to see only those, or pass `includeInactiveBookings=true` to see them alongside active bookings. |
| `bookingStatuses` | JsonElement? | no | Multi-status Resource Booking filter — JSON array of canonical names, e.g. ["Confirmed","FirstHold","SecondHold"] for active bookings. Records matching ANY listed status pass. Takes precedence over `bookingStatus` when both supplied. **Recommended over `bookingStatus` for 'who is working today / on-floor / scheduled' queries** — pass ["Confirmed","FirstHold","SecondHold"] to capture all real holds in one call instead of inferring `Confirmed` only. |
| `includeInactiveBookings` | bool | no | Include Cancelled and Released bookings in results. Default false (these statuses clutter the active-schedule view). Pass true ONLY when user EXPLICITLY mentions cancelled, released, inactive, or 'all bookings'. If `bookingStatus` is set explicitly (e.g. to 'Cancelled'), that takes precedence and this flag becomes irrelevant. |
| `onlyInactive` | bool | no | **Inverse mode** — return ONLY talents in the pool that have ZERO bookings overlapping [dateFrom..dateTo]. Use for 'who hasn't been booked recently' / 'inactive freelancers' / 'access cleanup' queries (e.g. 'which freelancers haven't been booked in 60+ days'). The pool is determined by the usual sources (talentCrewIds, sessionId, or the full studio crew). When set, the tool clears all booking/availability records before rendering, forces phantom emission, and bypasses status filters (bookingStatus*/availabilityStatus* become noise). Pair with `dateFrom=&lt;60d ago&gt;, dateTo=&lt;today&gt;` for the canonical use case. Skill / employmentType narrowing: chain via `query_talent_crew(employmentType=Freelancer, view=data)` first to get IDs, then pass as `talentCrewIds` here. Default false — normal mode returns talents WITH records. |
| `sessionId` | string | no | Filter bookings linked to a specific session — must be the session UUID. If the user gave a session code, name, or ambiguous identifier, you MUST first call `query_planning` (use `sessionCode` for explicit codes, `sessionName` for explicit names, `session` for ambiguous) to resolve it; pass the returned `id` here, and use `timeSlots` to set dateFrom + dateTo. Passing a non-UUID returns an error. |
| `bookingCreatedBefore` | string | no | ISO date — return only bookings created before this date (surface stale holds). |
| `groupByAvailabilityStatus` | bool | no | Aggregation: group by User Availability status and return counts. |
| `groupByBookingStatus` | bool | no | Aggregation: group by Resource Booking status and return counts. |
| `hasConflict` | bool | no | Health: return only talents with active overbooking conflicts (conflictStatusId 105/106/107). |
| `pageSize` | int | no | Max results in list mode (ignored in aggregation). Set to 0 for COUNT-only mode — response keeps `totalAvailabilities` + `totalBookings` (full counts after status/session filtering) but omits the item arrays. Use this when the user asks 'how many ...' without needing per-record details. |
| `view` | string | no | View mode: `widget` (default) renders the avatar table widget; `data` returns the same records under `data[]` with `hits=[]` (widget auto-hides) and SKIPS avatar resolution. **Use `view=data` ONLY when the result is being chained as input to another tool call (intermediate data extraction)**, NOT for user-facing answers. Example chain: extract talent IDs to feed into a follow-up query_asset(talentCrewId=...) call. Default `widget` is correct for ALL user-facing answers. |

</details>

**Example input**

```json
{ "dateFrom": "2026-06-10", "dateTo": "2026-06-20", "bookingStatus": "Confirmed", "pageSize": 10 }
```

**Example output**

```json
{ "total": 5, "hits": [ { "talentCrewId": "t-101", "displayName": "Jane Doe", "availabilityStatus": "Available", "bookingStatus": "Confirmed", "onSetRole": "Photographer", "hasConflict": false } ] }
```

**Known limitations**

Availability + bookings grouped by talent. Status is filtered in-memory (the planning backend has no status filter); skill is applied as a post-filter.

<a id="tool-query_team_on_set_skills"></a>
## `query_team_on_set_skills` — Query Team On Set Skills

List all team on set skills configured in the studio. Skills define roles that can be assigned to team members on productions (e.g. Photographer, Stylist, Model, Hair & Makeup, Art Director). Each skill belongs to a skill group (Photography, Talent). allowDoubleBooking: whether a team member with this skill can be booked on multiple sessions at the same time. isCustom: true = custom skill created by the studio, false = built-in system skill. A system skill (isCustom=false) CANNOT be renamed, re-grouped, or deleted — you may only change its double-booking setting. A custom skill (isCustom=true) can be renamed, re-grouped, have its double-booking toggled, or be deleted. Add-on skills whose subscription feature the studio does not have enabled (e.g. Videographer, Digital Processing, Post Review) are excluded, mirroring the Gamma Team On Set Skills page. Requires the Planning OR Resources subscription feature — returns an error when neither is enabled. Returns the full list in one call (no pagination).

- **CF module:** Studio Settings
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no

**Parameters**

_None._

**Example input**

```json
{}
```

**Example output**

```json
{ "total": 9, "items": [ { "name": "Photographer", "id": 1, "skillGroup": "Photography", "skillGroupId": 3, "allowDoubleBooking": false, "isEnabled": true, "isCustom": false } ] }
```

**Known limitations**

Team on set skills are roles assignable to team members on productions (Photographer, Stylist, Model, Hair & Makeup, Art Director, etc.). Takes NO params — full list in one call, no pagination. `id` is an int. Only Photography and Talent skill groups are returned; add-on skills whose subscription feature the studio lacks (Videographer, Digital Processing, Post Review) are excluded, mirroring the Gamma page. isCustom: true = studio-created, false = built-in. `allowDoubleBooking` = can be booked on overlapping sessions.

<a id="tool-query_workflow"></a>
## `query_workflow` — Query Workflow

List workflow definitions configured in the studio. A workflow definition is the production pipeline template (steps + branching) applied to jobs/products. Returns: id, name, workflowTypeId, workspace, isDefault, isEnabled, description, hasDraft, updated. **Use cases**: (1) Enumerate which workflows exist for a workspace. (2) Find the default/enabled workflow for a client. (3) Search workflows by name. Pass 'workspace' (name or ID) to scope to one client; omit to list across the studio. Pass 'keyword' for server-side partial name search. Sort: 'az' (A→Z), 'za' (Z→A), 'created' (creation date). By default raw ids are omitted for readability (no record id / version id). Pass 'includeIds=true' when the user wants ids — e.g. to then drill into a specific workflow with get_workflow_detail.

- **CF module:** Workflow
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|:--------:|-------------|
| `workspace` | string | no | Workspace/client name or ID to scope the list. Omit to list across the studio. |
| `keyword` | string | no | Search workflow by name (partial match, case-insensitive). Omit to list all. |
| `isEnabled` | bool? | no | Filter by enabled state. true = only enabled, false = only disabled. Omit for both. |
| `workflowTypeId` | int? | no | Filter by numeric workflow type id (content type). Omit for all types. |
| `sort` | string | no | Sort order: 'az', 'za', or 'created'. Default 'created'. |
| `pageSize` | int | no | Max results per page. Default 50. |
| `page` | int | no | Page (0-based). Default 0. |
| `includeIds` | bool | no | Include raw ids (record id, version id) and numeric workflowTypeId. Default false — human-readable fields only. Set true when the user asks for ids or you need the id to call get_workflow_detail. |

**Example input**

```json
{ "workspace": "Acme", "keyword": "apparel", "includeIds": true }
```

**Example output**

```json
{ "returned": 1, "hasMore": false, "workflows": [ { "id": "f14e694e-...", "name": "Apparel Std", "workspace": "Acme", "isEnabled": true } ] }
```

**Known limitations**

List/search workflow definitions (production pipeline templates) only — use get_workflow_detail to read one workflow's steps. The record id is omitted unless includeIds=true (needed to chain into get_workflow_detail). Returns both Published and Draft. Cursor pagination via lastOrderKey = page*pageSize; sort az/za/created. If WorkflowManagementUrl points at internal-backend it may return empty — the public gateway is required. workflowTypeId is emitted raw (no name lookup yet).


**Known limitations**

Returns workspace/client configuration only. Use the returned `id`s as the `workspace` filter on the other query tools.

<a id="tool-send_feedback"></a>
## `send_feedback` — Send Feedback

Send feedback to the Creative Force team. Types: result_feedback (rate a result), unsolved_question (couldn't get an answer), feature_request (want new capability).

- **CF module:** Platform
- **Read-only:** no · **Idempotent:** no · **Destructive:** no

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|:--------:|-------------|
| `type` | string | **yes** | Feedback type: result_feedback, unsolved_question, or feature_request |
| `message` | string | **yes** | Your comment, question, or request |
| `rating` | string | no | Rating (for result_feedback): correct, incorrect, or partial |
| `relatedToolName` | string | no | Which tool produced the result |
| `relatedToolInput` | string | no | Parameters used in the related tool call |
| `relatedToolOutput` | string | no | Summary of what the tool returned |

**Example input**

```json
{ "type": "result_feedback", "rating": "correct", "message": "Job list was accurate", "relatedToolName": "query_ecomm_job" }
```

**Example output**

```json
{ "status": "received", "type": "result_feedback" }
```

**Known limitations**

The only tool that writes anything — it sends your feedback to the Creative Force team and writes nothing to your studio's data.

<a id="tool-update_planning_session"></a>
## `update_planning_session` — Update Planning Session

Update an existing planning session (a scheduled production shoot). **This is a write** — it changes real data. It applies a TARGETED PARTIAL update: only the fields you pass change, everything else is left untouched. **FIND THE SESSION FIRST.** This tool takes a session **id** (UUID) — it does NOT search. Use the planning-session query tool to find the session first, then pass its `id`. **FOR CREW OR TIME-SLOT EDITS, PASS THE CURRENT STATE FROM THAT SAME QUERY.** This tool never reads the session itself, so for those two field groups you must give it the current state the query returned: for `crewOps`, copy the session's `team[]` straight into `currentTeamMembers` (keep each member's `userId`, `skillId`, `sessionTeamMemberId`); for `timeSlots`, pass the COMPLETE new slot list, keeping each retained slot's `sessionTimeSlotId` from the query result. (Scalars, customProperties and customResources need NO current state — they patch in place.) **CONFIRM BEFORE CALLING — but don't be repetitive.** Two conditions must hold before you call this tool: (1) the user has seen exactly what will change — every field you're about to update, and for crew the resulting team after the ops; and (2) the user has explicitly agreed to apply it. The GOAL is an informed yes, not a fixed script. So: if you've ALREADY laid out the specific changes in the conversation (e.g. you listed the production items / fields and the user replied "yes, all of them" / "go ahead"), that satisfies both conditions — do NOT re-print the same list as a separate "preview" block and ask a second time; just call the tool. Only build an explicit preview-and-confirm step when the changes haven't been spelled out yet, or the user's request is the FIRST mention and they haven't confirmed the specifics — then show the summary and ask a direct yes/no like "Shall I apply this update?" and WAIT. Never call it on a bare first request whose specifics the user hasn't seen and approved. (After you call it, the host also shows its own Allow/Deny prompt — a second, separate gate that does not replace getting the user's informed yes.) Accepts human-readable NAMES (production type, location, workspace, producer, crew people + skills) — resolved to IDs server-side. Pass each person as the user typed them (name, email, or id) — the tool resolves it, so there's no need to look an id up first, and a failed call tells you exactly how to fix the arguments. **Writes fail hard on unresolved names**: if a person can't be matched to exactly one user, or a skill isn't a valid allowed skill the person possesses, the tool returns an error and changes nothing. **Clearing fields:** to remove the location pass `location`="No set"; to remove the producer pass `producer`=""; to reset the card color pass `color`="none"; to switch a session to editorial pass `productionType`="editorial". **crewOps** is a list of delta operations on the current team — { op:"add", person, skill? } (skill OPTIONAL — omit it or pass "none" to add the person without a skill yet), { op:"remove", person }, { op:"changeSkill", person, skill } (pass skill "none" to clear it). There's no swap — express it as remove + add. Each op fails hard if it's inconsistent with `currentTeamMembers` (add a person already on the team, remove/changeSkill a person not on it). On success it returns `{ updated, sessionId, applied, changes }`: `applied` lists which field groups were written, and **`changes` is the authoritative per-field result you should report to the user** — each field you changed appears with its new value, and a removed field shows the literal "cleared" (e.g. `changes.producer = "cleared"`). **Verify the outcome from `changes` in this response — do NOT re-query the session just to confirm a change landed** (the read model can lag a just-written change).

- **CF module:** Planning
- **Read-only:** no · **Idempotent:** no · **Destructive:** no

**Parameters**

<details>
<summary>Show all 17 parameters</summary>

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|:--------:|-------------|
| `sessionId` | string | no | REQUIRED. The session id (UUID) to update — obtained from a prior planning-session query's `id` field. This tool does not resolve names or codes; pass a UUID. |
| `name` | string | no | New session name. Sparse — only sent if provided. |
| `description` | string | no | New description. Sparse. Max ~2000 chars. |
| `location` | string | no | New set/location name or id. Pass 'No set' to CLEAR the location. Sparse. |
| `productionType` | string | no | New production type: a shooting-type name/id, OR the literal 'editorial' to switch the session to editorial. Sparse. |
| `workspace` | string | no | New workspace/client name or id. Sparse. |
| `producer` | string | no | New producer — user name, email, or id. Must resolve to exactly one user. Pass an empty string to CLEAR the producer (remove it). Sparse — omit to leave the producer unchanged. |
| `color` | string | no | Session-card color — one of the 12 fixed colors (Google-Calendar palette). Pass the color NAME (preferred) or its numeric id 0-11. Map the user's everyday color words to the closest name using this guide: `tomato`(11) = red; `flamingo`(4) = pink / light red / coral; `tangerine`(10) = orange; `banana`(1) = yellow; `sage`(9) = light/pale green; `basil`(2) = dark green; `peacock`(8) = teal / cyan / turquoise; `blueberry`(3) = blue / dark blue; `lavender`(7) = light purple / lilac; `grape`(5) = purple / violet; `graphite`(6) = gray; `bright`(0) = white / default (no tint). E.g. "make it red" → `tomato`; "blue" → `blueberry`; "teal"/"turquoise" → `peacock`; "purple" → `grape` (or `lavender` if they say light purple). If the user names a color exactly (e.g. "tomato"), use it as-is. Pass "none"/"reset"/empty to RESET to no manual color. Sparse — omit to leave the color unchanged. |
| `timeZone` | string | no | Session timezone — an IANA name (e.g. 'Asia/Tokyo'). Affects how bare datetimes in `timeSlots` are interpreted; also sent with the slot upsert. Defaults to the user's timezone. **To CHANGE the session's timezone while keeping the same clock times** (e.g. 'move this shoot to Tokyo time' — 9am stays 9am, now Tokyo): set `timeZone` to the new tz, set `currentTimeZone` to the session's existing tz, and pass the session's CURRENT timeSlots back unchanged (the absolute/UTC times from the query). The tool then keeps each slot's wall-clock and recomputes it under the new tz, exactly like the app's Change-timezone action. |
| `currentTimeZone` | string | no | The session's CURRENT timezone (IANA name or tz id), copied from the planning-session query. Pass this ONLY when you're changing `timeZone` to a different value AND want the existing clock times preserved (the timezone-change case described under `timeZone`). When set, the tool reads each retained slot's wall-clock in this old timezone and re-interprets it in the new `timeZone`. Omit it if you're sending fresh slot times (bare datetimes) rather than rebasing the existing ones. |
| `timeSlots` | JsonElement? | no | The COMPLETE new time-slot list (full-array replace). JSON array of { sessionTimeSlotId?, start, end }: keep each retained slot's `sessionTimeSlotId` from the query result; omit it on a new slot; drop a slot entirely to delete it. `start`/`end` are ISO datetimes carrying their own day (see create tool). **Each slot must start and end on the SAME calendar day** (in the session timezone) — a single slot CANNOT span two days, and the tool rejects one that does (e.g. 7 Jul → 8 Jul is invalid). **When the user gives a continuous range that CROSSES MIDNIGHT, you MUST SPLIT it at midnight into TWO slots — do NOT clamp the end back to the first day, and do NOT drop the after-midnight part.** Split so no requested time is lost: first slot = start → 23:59 of the start day, second slot = 00:00 of the next day → the user's end time. Example — 'from 17:00 on 7 Jul to 02:00 on 8 Jul' → [{"start":"2026-07-07T17:00","end":"2026-07-07T23:59"},{"start":"2026-07-08T00:00","end":"2026-07-08T02:00"}]. A slot needs start &lt; end, so if the after-midnight part is zero-length (the range ends exactly at 00:00), drop the second slot and keep just [{"start":"2026-07-07T17:00","end":"2026-07-07T23:59"}]. Before sending, tell the user you've split the overnight range into two slots and confirm. **A MULTI-DAY session is likewise expressed as one slot PER DAY**: a shoot running 7–8 Jul 09:00–17:00 → TWO slots [{"start":"2026-07-07T09:00","end":"2026-07-07T17:00"},{"start":"2026-07-08T09:00","end":"2026-07-08T17:00"}], NOT one slot from 7 Jul to 8 Jul. Omit this param to leave time slots untouched. |
| `crewOps` | JsonElement? | no | Delta operations on the crew. JSON array of { op, person, skill? }. op = 'add' (skill required), 'remove', or 'changeSkill' (skill required). `person` = a name, email, or userId. For **remove**, the simplest is to pass the member's `userId` from `currentTeamMembers` (it's matched directly against the team). For **add**/**changeSkill**, pass a name or email (the tool looks up the person's skills to validate the new skill). **Skill is OPTIONAL on add** — omit it or pass `skill`:"none" to put someone on the team without a skill yet. To CLEAR an existing member's skill, use changeSkill with `skill`:"none". E.g. [{"op":"add","person":"Anna","skill":"Stylist"},{"op":"add","person":"Le Ngan"},{"op":"changeSkill","person":"Carl","skill":"none"},{"op":"remove","person":"&lt;userId&gt;"}]. REQUIRES `currentTeamMembers`. |
| `currentTeamMembers` | JsonElement? | no | The session's current crew, copied straight from the planning-session query's `team[]`. JSON array of { userId, skillId, sessionTeamMemberId }. Required whenever `crewOps` is given — the tool applies the ops to this list and sends the full result. (Booking/hold status is NOT touched by this tool — it's managed by a separate booking-status flow — so you don't need to pass it.) |
| `customProperties` | JsonElement? | no | Custom properties to set (true sparse patch — only the named ones change). JSON array of { name, value }. E.g. [{"name":"Campaign","value":"Winter"}]. Values are validated against the property's type: a **Number** property needs a numeric value within ±99999999999.9999; a **Free text** property is capped at 2048 characters; a **List of options** property needs one of its defined options (case-insensitive) — a bad value returns an error listing the allowed options. Dates take ISO (e.g. '2026-06-24'). |
| `customResources` | JsonElement? | no | Custom resources to add/change — free-form (label, person) production-support roles (catering, driver, runner…). JSON array of { label, name }. The tool reads the session's current resources itself and overlays these by label, so pass only what changes. (Setting `name` to empty keeps the row with no person — it does NOT delete the row; to delete a row use `removeCustomResources`.) |
| `removeCustomResources` | JsonElement? | no | Custom resources to DELETE — a JSON array of labels to remove entirely from the session, e.g. ["Driver","Catering"]. The tool drops these from the session's resource set and writes the rest. Use this (not an empty `name` in `customResources`) when the user wants a resource row gone. |
| `productionItemOps` | JsonElement? | no | Assign / remove / move PRODUCTION ITEMS (work units) to/from this session — the assignment link only; it never changes the production item's own workflow or status. JSON array of { op, productionItemIds }, where op is 'add', 'remove', or 'move' and `productionItemIds` is an ARRAY of ids (so 'add all 12 work units of this job' is ONE op). **Get the ids from the production query tool first**, then preview which production items you'll assign and get a yes. **WHICH ID TO PASS depends on the session's content type:** for an **e-comm** (shooting-type) session, pass the work unit's `id` from query_ecomm_production. for an **editorial** session, pass the **`deliverableId`** taken from query_editorial_production's `deliverableOfFinalize.deliverableId` field. **Do NOT pass the editorial work unit's top-level `id` — editorial assignment uses the deliverableId, and a work-unit id will be rejected as non-existent.** **add vs move — choose by the production item's CURRENT state, NOT by the user's verb** (users say 'move' loosely): use **add** for a production item that isn't on any session yet (the common case); use **move** ONLY when the user names/implies the production item is currently on ANOTHER session ('from session A', 'on yesterday's shoot', 'it's on the wrong session') — move re-homes it here. When unsure, use **add**; if the backend reports an id was already on another session, the tool's warning tells you to retry that id with 'move'. Examples: 'Add the Nike hoodie work unit to this session' → add; 'Move these work units into session X' (no source named) → add; 'Move the hoodie work unit FROM session A to here' → move. **PRODUCTION-TYPE RULE (must hold for add/move):** every production item you assign MUST have the SAME production type / shooting type as the planning session's own production type. A session holds items of ONE production type only — e.g. a flat/still work unit cannot go on an on-model session, and you cannot mix two different production types in one call. Check each item's production type against the session's before assigning; if they differ, don't assign it — tell the user which items don't match instead. E.g. [{"op":"add","productionItemIds":["&lt;id1&gt;","&lt;id2&gt;"]},{"op":"move","productionItemIds":["&lt;id3&gt;"]}]. Best-effort: production-type-mismatched / already-assigned ids come back as a warning, the rest still apply. |

</details>

**Example input**

```json
{ "sessionId": "p1a2b3c4-d5e6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "name": "Holiday Campaign", "crewOps": [ { "op": "add", "person": "Anna Lee", "skill": "Stylist" } ], "currentTeamMembers": [ { "userId": "u1...", "skillId": 3, "sessionTeamMemberId": "tm1..." } ], "color": "tomato", "productionItemOps": [ { "op": "add", "productionItemIds": [ "wu1...", "wu2..." ] } ] }
```

**Example output**

```json
{ "updated": true, "sessionId": "p1a2b3c4-d5e6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "applied": [ "scalars", "crew", "products" ], "changes": { "name": "Holiday Campaign", "color": "tomato", "teamMembers": [ { "person": "Anna Lee", "skill": "Stylist", "userId": "u1..." } ], "productionItemsAdded": [ "wu1...", "wu2..." ] } }
```

**Known limitations**

Write tool — targeted partial update; only the fields you pass change. Id-only (find the session with query_planning first). For crew/time-slot edits pass the current state from that query (`currentTeamMembers` / `timeSlots` with their ids) — the tool never re-reads the session. Production items: `productionItemOps` assigns/removes/moves existing production items (work units) — the assignment link only, never the item's own workflow/status (get ids from query_ecomm_production; op add for an unassigned item, move only when it's on another session); production-type compatibility is enforced by the backend and rejected ids come back as a warning. Clears via a sentinel string (location "No set", producer "", color "none"). Verify from the returned `changes` map — do NOT re-query. Booking/hold status is NOT settable (separate flow, blocked by CPD-554). Requires McpWritePlanning (Access) + PlanningView (Write).
